subs: NebulaChaos: a correctness lab for my Raft cluster, NebulaOS.
Part 2 of the series. Part 1 showed it survives crashes.
NebulaOS heals from a leader crash in 3.2 seconds.
But surviving a crash is not the same as staying correct.
So I built a tester whose only job is to make the cluster lie.
Five real NebulaOS processes, a proxy on each of the 20 network links.
Clients read, write and compare-and-set while the nemesis breaks things.
Every operation is recorded, then checked: could one correct machine have done this?

data.title: Stale reads — with zero faults
data.lead: Upstream NebulaOS answered every read from the local replica of whichever node you asked.

subs: Bug 1. First run against upstream NebulaOS.
nebulachaos run: 10 clients, and the leader is cut off twice.
Real output, sped up. The checker reads all 9,000 operations.
Not linearizable, on every key.

segments.label: upstream NebulaOS
subs: A replay of that exact run, 0.16 s in. No fault injected yet.
write 7.5 is acknowledged. Then a read on n2 returns the older 5.3.
A follower answered from its own copy, one heartbeat behind the leader.

data.title:
ReadIndex on the leader,
a read barrier on followers
data.lead: Confirm leadership with a quorum heartbeat sent after the read arrived (Raft thesis §6.4), then serve once that index is applied.

subs: The fix: the ReadIndex protocol from Ongaro's Raft thesis.
Same schedule, same seed, fixed build.
Linearizable. 10 of 10 runs failed before the fix, 0 of 10 after.

data.title: One flipped bit erased acknowledged writes
data.lead: Writes land on a bare majority. Two of those nodes crash. One bit rots on the third.

subs: Bug 2. Under the first post, Ram pointed at durability. So I went after the disk.

segments.label: before the recovery fix
subs: n4 and n5 are cut off. Only n1, n2 and n3 acknowledge writes.
n1 and n3 crash. One bit flips in n2's Raft log.
n2 silently drops 72 log entries, then wins an election with n4 and n5.
An acknowledged write is gone: a later read returns the older value.

data.title: Refuse to start on damaged storage
data.lead: A bad record followed by intact records is corruption, not a torn write. Snapshot headers are checksummed too.

subs: The fix: tell corruption apart from a torn write, and refuse to start.

segments.label: after the fix
subs: Same schedule after the fix: n2 refuses to start.
No quorum for 7.6 s until n1 and n3 return. Unavailable, never wrong.

data.title: A successful write reported as failed
data.lead: A leader dies mid-request. The node retries. The command runs twice.

subs: Bug 3 needed leader churn: the leader is killed every two seconds.

segments.label: before the exactly-once fix
subs: Leaders keep dying while 20 clients write through every node.
A client is told "cas mismatch", yet a read returns the very value that CAS wrote.
Fix: a request id assigned once, so a retried command is applied at most once.

subs: Is the checker any good? I planted four known Raft bugs behind flags.
It caught three. The fourth needs millisecond timing: a job for deterministic simulation.

stats: operations in 60 random fault runs, all linearizable

subs: Each bug, on the same fault schedules, before and after its fix.
After the fixes: 60 randomized fault runs, 284,732 operations, all linearizable.
The protocol was fine. The bugs lived in the plumbing around it.
